[ASSISTANT_SAID] Medical professionals have studied cases of people who claim to have died and come back to life, known as near-death experiences (NDEs).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Many medical professionals have documented cases and conducted research on NDEs, including experiences such as out-of-body experiences, seeing a tunnel, a bright light, or meeting deceased loved ones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some studies have found that NDEs can have a profound impact on a person's mental and emotional well-being.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The scientific explanation for NDEs is still not fully understood; some researchers attribute them to chemical changes in the brain, while others believe they may be a gateway to the afterlife or spiritual realm.  
[USER] The user questions whether NDEs are just a hoax or hallucination, citing the lack of scientific proof of an afterlife or spiritual realm.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] NDEs are often attributed to physiological and psychological factors, such as oxygen deprivation, altered states of consciousness, or abnormal brain activity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some researchers argue that NDEs could be hallucinations or illusions created by the brain to cope with trauma and stress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are unexplained aspects of NDEs, such as meeting deceased loved ones, feeling peace or joy, and having a life review.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Further research is needed to fully understand the nature of NDEs and their implications for life and death.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important to approach the study of NDEs with an open mind and skepticism.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some aspects of NDEs can be explained by physiological factors, but others are difficult to explain, such as verifiable out-of-body experiences.
